Finally the design system gets a new rule: components specify their behaviour at three text scales in the component library, and a component is not complete until all three states exist. This moves the work from one-off fixes in screens to the shared parts, and stops the same defect being fixed ten times.
acceptanceCriteria: No clipped or overlapping text at the largest accessibility size
Primary buttons wrap instead of truncating
Touch targets are at least 44 by 44 points
Ten reference screens have golden images

items.title: Focus order skips the forgot-password link
items.description:
Using a keyboard or a switch device, Tab moves from the password field straight to the Sign in button and the Forgot your password link is never focused. The link is laid out before the button visually but added to the hierarchy after it, and the focus order follows the hierarchy.

A sweep of the other screens with a keyboard found two more where visual and focus order differ. The shared form layout now takes its focus order from the same list as the visual order, so they cannot diverge.
acceptanceCriteria: Tab visits the link between the password field and the button
items.reproSteps:
1. Connect a hardware keyboard to an Android tablet.
2. Open the sign-in screen.
3. Press Tab repeatedly.
4. The link is never highlighted.

items.title: High contrast theme
items.description: A separate theme with stronger colours for people with low vision. Removed after the audit showed the standard theme already meets the AA contrast ratio everywhere, and the system high contrast switch is respected by the standard theme.

items.title: Release and analytics
items.description:
Getting builds to testers and users safely, and learning what happens after they arrive.

The goal is a boring release train: a weekly candidate, a staged rollout and an obvious way back. Everything that makes shipping scary gets automated or deleted.

items.title: Weekly release train with staged rollout
items.description: Replace ad hoc releases with a fixed weekly cadence: a release candidate is cut every Monday, tested through the week and rolled out in stages on Thursday. The train leaves on time with whatever is ready; unfinished work waits for the next one. This gives support and marketing a date they can plan around and keeps changes small enough to reason about.
acceptanceCriteria: A candidate is cut every Monday
Rollout starts on Thursday at one percent
Unfinished work never delays the train

items.title: Set up beta distribution for both platforms
items.description:
Stand up the internal and external beta tracks so every merge to the main branch produces a build testers can install within half an hour. CI signs the iOS build with a distribution profile held in the secret store and the Android build with the upload key, then uploads and posts the link in the team channel.

Testers are organised in two groups: the staff group, who receive every build, and a public group that receives weekly candidates. Each build shows the commit and the date in the settings footer, which saves a lot of back and forth with testers about which version they run.

Release notes are generated from merged pull request titles, grouped by area, and edited by hand before the weekly candidate goes out. Rollbacks are handled by promoting the previous build rather than rebuilding it.

A staged rollout of the store release starts at one percent and moves to ten, fifty and one hundred percent over a week, pausing automatically if the crash-free rate drops below the agreed threshold. The thresholds are part of the checklist the release manager follows, and the dashboard that shows them is linked from the channel topic.

One caution from the previous project: store review times are not under our control, so the release checklist starts the review on Tuesday for a Thursday rollout, and hotfixes use the expedited path only when a security problem or a crash affecting more than one percent of sessions is confirmed.
acceptanceCriteria: Every merge to main yields an installable beta within thirty minutes
Staff and public tester groups exist
The build number and commit show in the settings footer
Staged rollout pauses below the crash-free threshold

items.title: Analytics events for the sign-in funnel
items.description:
Instrument the steps from opening the app to reaching the home feed so we can see where people drop: screen shown, field focused, submit pressed, error returned, and success. Every event carries the platform, app version and flow variant but never the email address or any token.

Event names follow a verb-object convention and are defined in one table that generates the constants for both platforms and the schema for the warehouse, which prevents the two apps drifting apart. A lint step rejects events not in the table.

The errors event needs a coarse reason from a fixed list: wrong credentials, network, locked, two-factor required, unknown. Free-form messages are not allowed because they leak details and explode the number of distinct values.

Funnels are built in the dashboard for password, Apple, Google and biometric entries separately, since the drop-off points differ. Consent is read before any event is sent; people who opted out of analytics produce only anonymous, aggregated counters of crashes, and nothing else.

The first report we promised is the share of people who reach the home feed within two minutes of installing, split by entry method. Product will use it to decide whether the reset flow or the social buttons deserve the next sprint.

Data quality gets its own check: a nightly job compares the number of submit events with the number of sign-in requests the server saw, per platform and version. A gap above two percent opens an issue automatically, because a quiet instrumentation bug can mislead the team for weeks before anyone notices it.
acceptanceCriteria: All funnel steps emit events with platform and version
Event names come from one generated table
Errors use a fixed list of reasons
Opted-out users send no analytics events
A dashboard shows the funnel per entry method

items.title: Ask people on very old versions to upgrade
items.description:
When the server decides that the app version is below the minimum it supports, the app shows a full-screen message with an Update button that opens the store page and no way past it. A softer dismissible prompt appears when a recommended version is available. The decision comes from a small config endpoint called on launch with a short timeout, and a failed call never blocks the app.

The messages are plain: what changed, why it matters, and that their data is safe. Security fixes are named as the reason when they are the reason. We do not use the forced screen for design changes or features.

To avoid locking out people with no store access, the check is skipped for builds in the beta tracks and for versions released in the last seven days, which the store may not have rolled out to the person yet.

In the config the minimum and recommended versions are set per platform, and a kill-switch can disable the check altogether if we ever publish a bad minimum by mistake. The wording for both screens is translated into all launch languages before the first release that contains this story.

We also considered a server-driven approach that gates single features instead of the whole app. It was set aside as too large for this story, but the config endpoint is shaped so that a list of feature gates can be added later without changing the apps that already call it.
acceptanceCriteria: An unsupported version sees a blocking update screen
A recommended update shows a dismissible prompt
A failed config call never blocks the app
Beta builds and fresh releases skip the check
A kill-switch disables the check

items.title: Tablet layout with a side navigation rail
items.description: Two-pane layout for tablets with a navigation rail. Removed from this cycle by product: tablets are under two percent of sessions, and the phone layout scales acceptably on them for now.

items.title: Extract and translate all user-visible strings
items.description:
Move hard-coded strings in both apps into the string tables, add plural forms where counts appear and send the files to the translation vendor for German, Spanish, French and Japanese. Reject new hard-coded strings in review with a lint rule. Dates and numbers use the platform formatters with the person's locale, never hand-built patterns.

The vendor returns strings within two working days. Context screenshots are attached to each key so that translators can see where a word appears, which settled arguments about the meaning of Mute and Hold.
acceptanceCriteria: No visible hard-coded strings remain
Plurals are handled in all four languages
A lint rule blocks new hard-coded strings
